uncited: Per-Instance Attribute Buffering is a method for supplying per-instance data to vertex shaders by leveraging standard graphics API mechanisms other than the dedicated hardware instancing SSBO lookup.
The method consists of three distinct sub-techniques, each utilizing a different buffer type to store per-instance attributes.
The vertex shader receives this data either as uniform arrays or vertex attributes, eliminating the need for explicit instance ID lookups.
The application must manage buffer splitting if data exceeds the limit.
The instance index is used as the texture coordinate.
Each instance is treated as a distinct vertex or a set of vertices with associated attributes.
**Data Preparation:** Encode per-instance data into the chosen buffer type (Uniform, Texture, or Vertex Buffer).
**Buffer Binding:** Bind the buffer to the appropriate shader stage (Uniform Block, Texture Unit, or Vertex Attribute Array).
*   *Uniform:* Shader reads from uniform arrays.
*   *Texture:* Shader fetches texels using instance-derived coordinates.
*   *Vertex Buffer:* Hardware automatically loads attributes into registers; shader accesses them as standard vertex attributes.
Best for small datasets (<64KB) due to simplicity.
Useful when data fits well into texture formats or when uniform limits are hit.
Best for large datasets limited only by video memory.
*   **Time Complexity:** $O(1)$ per vertex for data access (hardware registers) or $O(1)$ for uniform/texture lookups.
No dynamic branching for instance ID calculation.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Proportional to the number of instances and data size per instance.
Uniform buffers are fast but limited in size.
Texture buffers add encoding/decoding overhead.
It represents an alternative to dedicated instancing mechanisms by utilizing existing buffer types.
